This is a specific, verifiable architecture/scope inconsistency in the new sync mechanism, not an incorrect-behavior defect.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts (lines 72-91), the code directly calls fetch to 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token' for token refresh, then uses parseRefreshTokenResponse. However, unlike other integrations (Google Calendar, Office365, Zoom, Webex, etc.) which wrap their refresh calls in refreshOAuthTokens(), Salesforce does NOT use refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (shown in the diff at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) checks APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and routes to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT when enabled. Since Salesforce bypasses this wrapper, it won't participate in the credential sync feature that this PR is implementing, which is inconsistent with the stated purpose of the changes.
